items.title: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
items.topic: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
items.summary: MoRAL, a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline developed by the authors, teaches Cosmos-Reason2-2B to read a physics-encoded Bird's Eye View (BEV) representation and reason over it for driving decisions, with the BEV image encoding LiDAR metric distance, object class, and radar Doppler velocity, allowing for reliable metric grounding and compact model size, achieving zero-shot baselines on 60,000 grounding records. This approach enables the model to make driving decisions based on the encoded information. The use of BEV representation and physics-encoded information enhances the model's ability to reason about the environment. MoRAL's performance is significant for autonomous driving applications, where compact and reliable models are crucial.

items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: CommandLM, a multimodal large language model introduced by the researchers, generates concise, human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data, processing temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model, achieving CIDEr 0.67 and BERT-F1 0.88 on the CommandLM-nuScenes dataset. This model is essential for safety, trust, and regulation in autonomous driving systems. The CommandLM model's performance is notable, given its ability to produce intent-aware and interpretable captions. The use of a Q-Former adapter and LoRA-fine-tuned large language model contributes to the model's strong linguistic and behavioral alignment.

items.title: TALSC: Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration for Infrastructure-Assisted Autonomous Driving
items.topic: TALSC: Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration for Infrastructure-Assisted Autonomous Driving
items.summary: TALSC, a Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration framework developed by the authors, balances the accuracy gains of large VLMs with their latency-induced timeliness degradation, modeling the Age of Information (AoI) evolution for VLM inference and characterizing the coupling between AoI and inference accuracy, enabling collaboration between large and small VLMs in infrastructure-assisted autonomous driving. This framework is crucial for addressing the resource constraints of on-board computing power in autonomous vehicles. The TALSC framework's ability to model AoI evolution and characterize the coupling between AoI and inference accuracy is significant for autonomous driving applications. The use of large and small VLMs in collaboration enhances the overall performance of the system.
